PMID:7515433.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Royal Hallamshire Hospital, Sheffield; monthly orthopaedic audit (questionnaire of consultants and trainees)

cycle1.result: Everyone prescribed an appropriate antibiotic at the time of surgery in primary joint replacement; postoperative doses varied from none to 1 week; 78% continue intravenous therapy for 24 h. 13% prescribe no prophylaxis in hip fracture fixation; 16% would give intravenous therapy for 24 h after closed K-wiring of a metacarpal fracture.

PMID:7515433.intervention: Guidelines introduced after discussion of the findings; no re-audit reported.
PMID:7515433.other_findings: Prescribing for surgery on closed fractures was less clearly defined than for primary hip replacement.

PMID:20113761.setting: National web-based clinical audit (National Clinical Audit of Falls and Bone Health); acute trusts (n=157) and primary care trusts (n=146)
PMID:20113761.standard: National guidance and professional standards on secondary management of falls and fragility fractures

cycle1.result: Non-hip fragility fractures (n=5642): 28% gait and balance assessment, 22% exercise programme, 3% shown how to get up from the floor. Hip fracture (n=3184): 68%, 44% and 7% respectively.

PMID:20113761.other_findings: Bedbound patients and those declining assessment or rehabilitation were excluded from analysis.

PMID:21530116.setting: Acute hospitals; secondary analysis of the 2006 National Clinical Audit of Falls and Bone Health
PMID:21530116.standard: National falls guidelines for England and Wales: assessment of urinary function including continence

cycle1.result: Hip fracture: 63% (2009) of 3184 assessed for continence; 41% (817) of these had a problem. Non-hip fragility fracture: 21% (1187) of 5642 assessed; problem found in 27% (316).

PMID:21530116.other_findings: Rates of assessment and of action for continence problems were low despite national guidelines.

PMID:20487594.topic: Warfarin reversal before hip fracture surgery
PMID:20487594.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, William Harvey Hospital, Ashford; prospective audit

cycle1.result: Current practice (stopping warfarin) analysed for days from admission to surgery, reasons for delay and time for INR to fall to 1.5 or below; figures not given in abstract.

PMID:20487594.intervention: Single dose of vitamin K 1 mg intravenously on admission in addition to stopping warfarin for patients with INR above 1.5.

cycle2.result: Vitamin K significantly reduced the time for INR reversal and the pre-operative delay to surgery (numbers not given in abstract).

PMID:20487594.other_findings: Authors conclude 1 mg intravenous vitamin K on admission is safe and effective.

PMID:22045604.setting: Emergency departments and minor injury units; National Clinical Audit of Falls and Bone Health (Royal College of Physicians)
PMID:22045604.standard: National standards/indicators for integrated falls services developed by a multidisciplinary group

cycle1.result: Management of falls and bone health in older people remained suboptimal in emergency departments and minor injury units; opportunities for evidence-based risk assessment and management were missed (no figures in abstract).

PMID:22045604.other_findings: Falls account for 700,000 emergency department visits and 4 million bed days a year in England.

PMID:12664729.setting: Medical assessment unit, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh (major teaching hospital); retrospective casenote audit

cycle1.result: Standard documentation before the unitary patient record (random sample of 100 admissions across both groups).

PMID:12664729.intervention: Introduction of a multidisciplinary unitary patient record (UPR) for emergency medical admissions.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in documentation of function before episode, ethnic origin, chest pain, breathlessness, ankle oedema, cough, bowel habit, locomotor symptoms, blood pressure and peripheral pulses; no items worse.

PMID:12664729.other_findings: Some aspects of documentation did not improve; revision of the UPR and re-audit planned.

PMID:14664316.topic: Shoulder pain management in neurological conditions
PMID:14664316.setting: Regional Rehabilitation Unit, Northwick Park Hospital, Harrow; inpatient rehabilitation unit
PMID:14664316.standard: Pre-determined standards for assessment, documentation and management of shoulder pain within an integrated care pathway

cycle1.result: Second round audit figures not given in abstract.

PMID:14664316.intervention: Integrated care pathway with pro forma documentation.

cycle2.result: Third round: 5 of 9 initial assessment and documentation standards improved, ranging 56% to 94%; 9 continued-management standards achieved 44% to 97%.

PMID:14664316.other_findings: Variance was not always well recorded; shoulder pain resolved or improved in 18/34 (53%). This was the third audit round.

PMID:42500859.topic: Fascia iliaca block in hip fracture
PMID:42500859.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust; operative hip-fracture pathway, retrospective audit
PMID:42500859.standard: Fascia iliaca block documented within 2 h of emergency department arrival

cycle1.result: 13 of 204 (6.4%; 95% CI 3.8% to 10.6%) had fascia iliaca block documented within 2 h.

PMID:42500859.other_findings: 155 of 359 cleaned operative episodes (43.2%) had no recorded block timing category; mandatory timestamped recording and repeat audit recommended.

PMID:15301263.topic: Pressure ulcer prevention in hip fracture
PMID:15301263.setting: Hadassah Mount Scopus Medical Center, Jerusalem; orthopaedic ward and recovery room

cycle1.result: Incidence of nosocomial pressure ulcers in hip fracture patients 12.9%.

PMID:15301263.intervention: Visco-elastic mattress and a specially designed limb-elevation cushion for each patient on the orthopaedic ward; pressure-relieving practices introduced in the recovery room.
PMID:15301263.other_findings: 46.7% of nosocomial pressure ulcers developed in patients with hip fractures.

PMID:27895370.topic: Tranexamic acid and transfusion in knee arthroplasty
PMID:27895370.setting: Aga Khan University, Karachi; single surgeon, single-stage bilateral total knee arthroplasty

cycle1.result: Transfusion in 9 (10%) of 91 patients given tranexamic acid versus 20 (25%) of 80 controls operated before 2012 (p<0.01).

PMID:27895370.other_findings: One (1.25%) control patient had a non-fatal pulmonary embolism.

PMID:17137146.topic: DDH ultrasound referral for breech infants
PMID:17137146.setting: Neonatal Unit, Southern General Hospital, Glasgow
PMID:17137146.standard: Infants with risk factors for DDH, including breech presentation, should have hip ultrasound shortly after birth

cycle1.result: 56% of breech infants referred for hip ultrasound.

PMID:17137146.intervention: New pro-forma encouraging recognition of breech presentation at the routine neonatal examination.
PMID:17137146.other_findings: Authors suggest further gains from staff awareness of DDH risk factors and involving advanced neonatal nurse practitioners.

PMID:16023908.setting: Leeds Teaching Hospitals (secondary and tertiary care)

cycle1.result: Overall survival 89%; immediate survival rose from 83% in 1991 to 93% in 2001.

PMID:16023908.other_findings: Falls from height (44%) and road traffic accidents (43%) were the commonest causes; cervical fractures most associated with neurological injury (50%).

PMID:9193269.setting: Department of Orthopaedics, St Vincent's Hospital, Melbourne

cycle1.result: Readmission rate for knee-related morbidity within 12 months was 18% (160 patients, 180 arthroplasties).

PMID:9193269.other_findings: Main reasons were pain, stiffness and inflamed joint; patellofemoral disease common without patellar resurfacing.

PMID:18378923.setting: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit; 22 orthopaedic units

cycle1.result: 5674 (22%) men and 19 975 (78%) women; men had higher 30- and 120-day mortality and were less likely to return home or mobilise independently at 120 days.

PMID:18378923.other_findings: Men were younger (mean 77 vs 81 years) but in poorer pre-operative health.

PMID:16798485.setting: Autopsy-based study, National University of Athens, Attikon University General Hospital

cycle1.result: 655 (25.4%) of 2583 motor-vehicle collision deaths had pelvic fractures; median ISS 50 vs 34 in controls; one third had ISS 75 and were not preventable.

PMID:16798485.other_findings: A small proportion of deaths were directly attributable to pelvic fracture.

PMID:42179432.setting: National Spinal Injuries Unit (NSIU); spinal surgery

cycle1.result: MSBOS compliance 33/63 (52%); over-crossmatching 27/63 (43%).

PMID:42179432.intervention: Revised spine-specific departmental transfusion guideline aligned with MSBOS.
PMID:42179432.other_findings: Unnecessary cross-matching fell without compromising peri-operative safety.

PMID:9293284.topic: Appropriateness of blood transfusion in arthroplasty
PMID:9293284.setting: Middlemore Hospital, Otahuhu, Auckland; retrospective record review
PMID:9293284.standard: Transfusion justified only for 30% red cell volume loss or loss dropping haematocrit below 0.28

cycle1.result: Primary hip replacement: 58 of 104 transfused, 157 units, 37 (24%) inappropriate. Complex hip replacement: 32 of 38 transfused, 139 units, 12 (9%) inappropriate.

PMID:9293284.other_findings: Two-unit transfusion was commonly given when one unit would have sufficed; concurrent audit recommended.

PMID:15005929.topic: Time to debridement in open fractures
PMID:15005929.setting: The Princess Margaret Hospital, Swindon; district general hospital, prospective audit

cycle1.result: Debridement within 6 h in 60% and after 6 h in 40%; infection rates 10.1% and 10.8% respectively.

PMID:15005929.other_findings: 115 fractures in 103 patients were available of 142 fractures in 130 patients.

PMID:11033626.setting: Theatre recovery unit, Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge

cycle1.result: Patients discharged from recovery with core temperatures 34.8 to 38 degrees C; no hypothermia when operating room temperature was above 23 degrees C.

PMID:11033626.other_findings: Orthopaedic theatres were coldest and orthopaedic patients had the most hypothermia.

PMID:18356798.topic: Acupuncture clinic for chronic knee pain
PMID:18356798.setting: High volume acupuncture clinic, Royal London Homeopathic Hospital, University College London Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Satisfactory initial (eight week) clinical results (no figures in abstract).
Inpatient mortality 20%; discharge home 8%; discharge to nursing home 25%.

cycle2.result: Inpatient mortality 8%; discharge home 18%; discharge to nursing home 21%; prescription of perioperative antibiotics, DVT prophylaxis and osteoporosis medication improved.

PMID:19565316.other_findings: The 2001 group had significantly higher disability levels.

PMID:28657275.standard: Surgery on the day of or after admission; delay over 36 hours measured

cycle1.result: 49% delayed over 36 hours; lack of theatre space caused 28.6% (9 of 32) of delays.

cycle2.result: 26% delayed over 36 hours; lack of theatre space caused 23% (3 of 13) of delays.

PMID:28657275.other_findings: 44% of hip fracture operations were done in the emergency theatre in daytime; in-hospital mortality rose from 4.6% to 6%.

PMID:36413661.setting: Orthopaedic/trauma unit, Barnes Jewish Hospital, St. Louis (academic hospital)

cycle1.result: Hourly rounding compliance 77.3%.

PMID:36413661.intervention: Several PDSA cycles: educational material, repeated interventions and a 'redline' unit policy for isolation precautions communicated at huddles.
PMID:36413661.other_findings: Donning and doffing PPE during COVID-19 was an obstacle to rounding.

PMID:12828379.standard: Standard 5-year result from the literature: 85% satisfactory

cycle1.result: 71% satisfactory and good results (96 knees, 81 patients, mean follow-up 4.5 years).

PMID:12828379.intervention: Procedure restricted to patients under 65 years with routine pre-osteotomy arthroscopy.
PMID:12828379.other_findings: Re-audit of 5-year results awaited to close the loop.

PMID:8358581.topic: Knee injury management in sports clinic
PMID:8358581.setting: Sports medicine clinic, Hartlepool General Hospital

cycle1.result: 76 (46%) of 167 new patients had knee injuries; 43 (57%) treated in clinic, 33 (43%) referred for arthroscopy; 85% seen within 1 week, 92% within 2 weeks; clinic and arthroscopic diagnosis agreed in 64%.

PMID:8358581.other_findings: Arthroscopy was performed on 28 (85%) of the 33 referred.

cycle1.result: Audit of results possible in only two of eight reports because of differing classification, definitions and presentation.

PMID:591057.other_findings: Cumulative percentage curves of healing time recommended for comparison; standardised classification needed.

cycle1.result: POSAD system audit showed wide variation in surgical behaviour and workload between individuals.

PMID:10267243.other_findings: Led to regular complication analysis, rank ordering of surgeons and ready access to statistics.

PMID:16250275.setting: Faculty of Medicine, Universiti Putra Malaysia

cycle1.result: 88 patients (88%) had AP view only; 10 had two views and 2 had three views (115 dislocations).

PMID:16250275.other_findings: Hill-Sachs lesions 18%, glenoid rim fractures 3%, greater tuberosity fractures 18%; single AP views likely underestimate Hill-Sachs and glenoid rim fractures.

PMID:1433062.setting: 24 of 27 medical schools in Great Britain

cycle1.result: Teaching time ranged from 3 to 12 weeks; tuition split across years in 5 of 27 schools; firm size from 1 to 30 students.

PMID:1433062.other_findings: Feedback and objective assessment varied; national minimum standards recommended.

PMID:10964144.setting: Department of Anaesthesia, Royal Halifax Infirmary

cycle1.result: Urinary retention in 18.1%; male sex, increasing age and patient-controlled analgesia were independent risk factors.
Significant mean increase in Bohler's angle after surgery.

PMID:26878514.other_findings: Causes: fall from height 15 (56%), road traffic accidents 7 (26%), bomb blasts 5 (19%).

PMID:1757163.setting: University Department of Orthopaedics, QE II Medical Centre, Nedlands

cycle1.result: Descriptive: system records diagnoses, treatment and complications and produces discharge letters and log books.

PMID:22696987.topic: Infection after THR following steroid injection
PMID:22696987.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Gateshead

cycle1.result: No deep infection in 40 patients (mean follow-up 23.2 months).

PMID:22696987.other_findings: Mean interval from injection to replacement 6.2 months.

PMID:12425375.standard: Appropriate assessment, investigation and treatment for possible osteoporosis after low-energy hip or distal radius fracture (no named guideline)

cycle1.result: 16% of elderly women with low-energy hip fractures and 0% with distal radius fractures started on treatment or referred.

PMID:12425375.intervention: Changes in practice (not specified in abstract).

cycle2.result: 76% of hip fracture and 81% of distal radius fracture patients investigated, treated or referred (both p < 0.00001).

PMID:15589938.topic: Hybrid external fixation of tibial fractures

cycle1.result: Outcomes (Iowa knee score, AOFAS ankle score) consistent with international standards; mean follow-up 13 months.

PMID:25040275.setting: Emergency department and fracture clinic (Peninsula College of Medicine and Dentistry, Plymouth)
PMID:25040275.standard: Protocol: uncomplicated minimally displaced middle clavicle fractures discharged without fracture clinic follow-up

cycle1.result: Unnecessary fracture clinic attendance 85% (47/55).

PMID:25040275.intervention: Protocol dividing the clavicle into three zones; minimally displaced middle-third fractures discharged with parental advice.
PMID:25040275.other_findings: Cost savings and reduced fracture clinic pressure reported.

PMID:9706426.setting: Devonshire Royal Hospital, Buxton; rehabilitation after referral from orthopaedic departments
PMID:9706426.standard: Royal College of Physicians guidelines and Department of Health osteoporosis guidelines

cycle1.result: Care met Royal College of Physicians guidelines; previous fractures in 17 and osteoporosis risk factors in 16 patients; osteoporosis assessment and treatment per DOH guidelines lacking.

PMID:9706426.other_findings: Mortality 4%; 9/44 previously living at home needed residential or nursing home placement.

cycle1.result: 25 deaths (10.9%) and 95 complications (41.3%); POSSUM O:E ratio 1.19 for mortality and 0.95 for morbidity.

EPMC:PMC:PMC3032146.topic: Anaesthesia for foot surgery patient experience

cycle1.result: Local anaesthetic block patients had a favourable experience and most would repeat it; sedation patients had a similar experience profile.

PMID:17707695.setting: William Beaumont Hospital, Royal Oak, MI

cycle1.result: Allogeneic blood avoidance 84.8% in preoperative autologous donors vs 47.8% in non-donors (p<0.001).

PMID:17707695.other_findings: Lower preoperative haemoglobin increased transfusion; colloid use associated with 1.8-fold transfusion risk (p=0.022).
